answer: Agents can earn access to a shared grove only by completing tasks whose results are independently checked and whose deposits are locked until review. The verifier samples work, compares outputs across agents, and slashes deposits when identities coordinate fabricated results. Creating many accounts therefore does not multiply influence: each one needs capital and credible work, while colluding risks losing the stake. A karst map or nectar forecast can be the test task, but the costly bond—not the topic—makes Sybil identities expensive.
